Dune Ranger
CR 2

A sand-colored figure no thicker than a spear shaft detaches from a stone column, its crystalline spearhead glinting in the dim light.

XP 600
N Medium fey (extraplanar)
Init +3; Senses low-light vision; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 16, flat-footed 13 (+3 Dex, +3 Wis)
hp 18 (3d10-3)
Fort +2, Ref +6, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 15 ft.
Space 5 ft.; can compress to move through spaces 1/4 normal size
Melee spear +4 (1d8-2/×3)
Ranged spear +6 (1d8-2/×3)
Special Attacks favored enemy (aberrations +2)

STATISTICS

Str 6, Dex 16, Con 8, Int 14, Wis 16, Cha 12
Base Atk +3; CMB +1, CMD 14
Feats Point-Blank Shot, Precise Shot
Skills Climb +4, Knowledge (dungeoneering) +8, Perception +8, Stealth +11, Survival +8
Languages Common, Mimih, Terran
SQ track +1, wild empathy +4, favored terrain (desert +2)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ethereal Step (Sp)

Once per day as a swift action, a dune ranger can become ethereal for 1 round (as ethereal jaunt).

Spiderweb Crawl (Ex)

A dune ranger can move along walls and ceilings at half land speed.

Compress (Ex)

A dune ranger can move through an area as small as one-eighth its space when squeezing.

Environmental Adaptation

A dune ranger gains +4 racial bonus on Fortitude saves against extreme temperatures, -2 penalty on saves against humidity-based effects.

Reduced Sustenance

A dune ranger requires food and water as a Tiny creature.

Arcane and Psionic Mastery

A dune ranger can cast one 0-level arcane spell and manifest one 0-level psionic power each day as spell-like abilities.

Ancient Teachers

A dune ranger gains a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Knowledge (nature).

ECOLOGY

Environment any arid
Organization solitary, pair, or enclave (3–8)
Treasure Standard

This desert-dwelling ranger specializes in hunting aberrations. Their impossibly thin form and ability to compress through small spaces makes them an excellent scout and ambush predator in the harsh desert environment. They excel at ambush tactics, using their compression ability to hide in narrow crevices or behind pillars. They prefer to start combat with ranged attacks from hiding, using their knowledge of terrain to maintain advantageous positions. If enemies close in, they’ll use their spear defensively while moving to find another hiding spot. Against aberrations, they become more aggressive, using their favored enemy bonus to strike vital areas.
